EVS
Broadcast Systems Integration Brief

EVS Broadcast Equipment

The global standard for live sports production, slow-motion replay, and live content management. XS-VIA servers are the operational hub of virtually every major live sports OB truck and host broadcast facility.

Live Production Slow-Motion Replay IP Contribution SRT / NDI SMPTE ST 2110 REST API
← Back to Home

Platform Overview

EVS systems are hardware appliances — not software deployable on commodity servers. The XS-VIA runs a proprietary Linux-based OS and exposes both a file-based MXF/OP-1A output and a real-time API over Ethernet. Cerebrum is EVS's facility-level broadcast controller, managing not just EVS servers but third-party routers, multiviewers, and playout devices over a single unified control plane. Integration projects almost always involve the EVS LSM (Live Slow Motion) remote controller protocol alongside REST or IPLink XML.

Control API
REST + IPLink XML
Video I/O
ST 2110-20/30/40, 12G-SDI
File Format
MXF OP-1A / OP-Atom
IP Transport
SRT, NDI, Zixi
Controller
LSM remote, Cerebrum
Monitoring
SNMP v2c, syslog

Product Integration Briefs

Engineering detail on integration interfaces, protocol stacks, and real-world deployment constraints.

Live Production Server

XS-VIA Live Production Server

4U rack-mount hardware server for live ingest, slow-motion replay, and live content management. Supports up to 16 channels of 1080p at 50/60fps simultaneously. Standard in OB trucks and host broadcast facilities globally.

Architecture
Proprietary FPGA-based signal processing on custom PCIe cards. Linux host OS. Video essence stored on internal NVMe RAID — not accessible as a standard NAS share. External access via EVS IPLink or MXF file export only.
Video I/O
ST 2110-20 ST 2110-30 ST 2110-40 12G-SDI — ST 2110 requires a dedicated 25GbE NIC (Mellanox ConnectX-5 or certified equivalent). IP and SDI cannot be mixed on the same channel simultaneously.
Control API
EVS IPLink XML REST v1 — IPLink (TCP port 4500) is the legacy protocol used by LSM controllers and most third-party integrations. REST API (v1, HTTP port 8080) was introduced in 2023 for clip management and replay trigger.
AI Features
XtraMotion AI super slow-motion (frame interpolation to 8× slow) runs on an embedded GPU. Sports AI (automatic event detection) is delivered via the EVS Live Assist module — requires a separate server running EVS AI Engine connected over Ethernet.
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownPTP grandmaster must be an external hardware clock (GPS-disciplined). The XS-VIA cannot act as its own PTP grandmaster. In OB truck deployments without GPS lock, XS-VIA will accept PTP from a software grandmaster but timing jitter can cause intermittent frame drops under load — not always reproducible in testing.
Live Content Management

IPDirector

Windows client application for logging, searching, and managing content across multiple XS-VIA servers in real time. The primary tool for replay operators, highlight producers, and live archive teams at major sports events.

Architecture
Windows-only client (no web UI, no Linux). Communicates with XS-VIA servers via EVS proprietary TCP protocol (port 4500). SQL Server backend for production metadata. Multi-server management via EVS XNet shared bus.
APIs
EVS IPLink XML (TCP 4500) REST v1 MXF export — Third-party MAMs (Avid Interplay, Dalet) connect via the IPLink XML protocol or MXF file delivery over SMB/CIFS. Direct database access is not supported.
MAM Integration
Completed clips transfer to NAS via SMB share. The transfer service runs on a dedicated Windows server — not on the XS-VIA itself. Target MAM must watch the SMB drop folder and trigger ingest automatically; push notification from EVS is not available without the EVS Medialogg+ connector.
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownIPDirector runs as a 32-bit Windows application even in 2026. Antivirus software (particularly endpoint detection products) regularly quarantines IPDirector's DLLs on first installation. Whitelist the entire EVS install directory at the endpoint management layer before deployment.
Broadcast Facility Controller

EVS Cerebrum

Software-defined broadcast control system that manages signal routing, device control, and facility logic across mixed-vendor environments. Used in OB trucks, broadcast centres, and remote production hubs as the primary facility control layer.

Architecture
Windows Server application with a web-based control panel (HTML5). Driver model: each device type (router, multiviewer, XS-VIA, switcher) has a device driver loaded by the Cerebrum service. No container support — Windows Server bare-metal or VM only.
Protocols
NMOS IS-04 NMOS IS-05 REST API Ember+ (console control) — NMOS IS-04/IS-05 support means Cerebrum can discover and route ST 2110 sources alongside traditional SDI. Ember+ used for audio console (Lawo, SSL) integration.
Device Support
Native drivers for Ross Ultrix, Miranda/Grass Valley routers, Sony MVS switchers, Lawo audio consoles, Evertz multiviewers, and all EVS servers. Third-party devices without native drivers require a custom driver — EVS provides a Cerebrum driver SDK (C++ API).
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownCerebrum's device state database can diverge from actual device state after a device reboot if the device does not send an unsolicited state update. This affects primarily older SDI routers. Manual state refresh (right-click → resync in the device tree) is the only resolution until the router driver is updated.
UHD Live Production Server

EVS XT4K

The UHD successor to the XT3, targeting 4K/UHD sports production. Supports native 4K HDR workflows with HLG and PQ transfer functions alongside a backwards-compatible HD mode for mixed-resolution events.

Architecture
4U hardware appliance. 4K processing via updated FPGA pipeline. Up to 8 channels of 4K 50/60fps. 12G-SDI and ST 2110-20 UHD (4K) video I/O. NVMe RAID — same internal storage architecture as XS-VIA.
Video I/O
12G-SDI (4K) 3G-SDI (HD) ST 2110-20 UHD — 4K HDR: HLG (Hybrid Log-Gamma, ITU-R BT.2100) and PQ (ST 2084). SDR trims available via real-time LUT processing on board.
Control API
Same IPLink XML and REST v1 API as XS-VIA. All existing LSM controllers (LSM-VIA, Smart Controller) are XT4K-compatible without firmware update.
⚠ Integration Risk
KnownMixed 4K/HD production (XT4K + XS-VIA on the same EVS network) requires careful XNet bus bandwidth planning. 4K clips transferred over XNet at full resolution can saturate a 10GbE XNet segment during replays — always use dedicated XNet 25GbE for mixed-resolution facilities.
